sources.quote: REAL 3DO Interactive Multiplayer video game system
Disc tray Extended and retracted using the OPEN/CLOSE button.
Control port (CONTROLLER) Dedicated port for the 3DO control pad.
Low speed I/O: Dsub-9 pin xl

notes: Panasonic FZ-1 Operating Instructions, European PAL model (230-240 V AC, '© Matsushita Electric Industrial Co.. Ltd. 1994'), read from two archive.org scans of the same document: 'panasonic-3do-fz-1' (specifications, sockets) and 'panasonic-fz1-manual' (cleaner OCR for the power switch and OPEN/CLOSE lines); OCR text layer, primary. The manual adds 'Weight and dimensions are approximate.'
Axes labelled by Panasonic '(WXDXH)': body.width=284, body.depth=268, body.height=88. excludes_projections not stated: null. Mass 2.9 kg printed, recorded as 2900 g (a decimal shift).

ports and controls are the manual's 'Controls and Sockets Layout' (front and rear views). Not filed for want of a contract kind: 'Right/Left audio output socket (AUDIO OUT R/L)', the READY and ACCESS indicators. The layout shows no power socket and the power form is not stated: features.power_inlet null. The control port is a D-sub 9 ('Low speed I/O: Dsub-9 pin x1', OCR 'xl'), dedicated to the 3DO pad and daisy-chained: filed controller_de9 for its connector shape.

This is the PAL FZ-1. The North American FZ-1 (120 V) was not read; Computer History Museum 102674797 (FZ-1, 'Object consists of console, 5 control pads, antenna cable, and outer box') prints 11w x 3 1/4h x 10 1/2l (in) / 27.94w x 8.26h x 26.67l (cm) without saying which item was measured, so it is not filed and is not a conflict candidate; its weight '6 (lb)' is whole-pound. The record is used only for the role (museum tier).
external_ids: Wikidata Q229429 '3DO' (the platform item, API), igdb_platform from its P5795.
